base_member_text: [L14-L21] (MED/unterminated string handling) strlen returns zero rather than MAXSTRINGLEN when no NUL byte is present, causing a full nonterminated buffer to be misreported as empty.
audit_member_text: [L11-L21] (MED/string-validation) strlen returns zero both for an empty string and for a full 1024-byte array with no NUL terminator, so unterminated input is silently misinterpreted as empty.

base_member_text: [L30-L34] (HIGH/comparison logic) strcmp converts char_array1 into both string1 and string2, so it never compares the second input and always returns equality.
audit_member_text: [L27-L34] (HIGH/wrong-argument) strcmp constructs both string1 and string2 from char_array1, causing every comparison to report equality.

base_member_text: [L60-L68] (HIGH/buffer overflow) string_to_char_array does not reject or truncate input strings of length 1024 or greater, and writes the terminator at len_trim(string)+1 beyond its fixed 1024-element result.
audit_member_text: [L60-L68] (HIGH/bounds) string_to_char_array does not cap len_trim to MAXSTRINGLEN-1, so strings of length 1024 or more write beyond the result when data and the terminator are stored.

base_member_text: [L11-L21,L51-L58] (HIGH/buffer bounds contract) strlen and char_array_to_string unconditionally declare and scan a 1024-element input without accepting its actual length, so sequence-associated callers with shorter C buffers can be read out of bounds.

audit_member_text: [L30-L34] (LOW/semantic-contract) strcmp trims both converted strings and uses Fortran lexical comparison, which does not preserve ordinary C strcmp behavior for spaces preceding the NUL.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: For NUL-terminated inputs a and a followed by a space, the trimmed/blank-padded Fortran comparisons return equality rather than the C ordering. L31 additionally converts char_array1 again instead of char_array2, which is another error and does not neutralize the claimed trailing-space discrepancy.

audit_member_text: [L40-L49] (MED/unterminated-input) strcpy relies on the ambiguous zero returned by strlen, so an unterminated source copies only its first character and does not guarantee a terminator in the destination.
[L60-L68] (LOW/uninitialized-tail) string_to_char_array initializes only the payload and one terminator, leaving the remainder of its fixed 1024-element result undefined.
